title: Retrieval of the Best Counterargument without Prior Topic Knowledge
authors: Henning Wachsmuth; Shahbaz Syed; Benno Stein
task_description: Retrieve the best counterargument for an input argument under same-debate, same-theme, and whole-portal candidate pools.
inputs: Argument plus candidate counterarguments from iDebate; stance/topic context varies by retrieval setting.
outputs_or_labels: Binary true/false counterargument relevance pairs; train/validation/test splits.
artifact_access_status: verified dataset landing page; download linked from Webis/Zenodo
evidence_basis: Paper reports 6,753 argument/best-counterargument pairs and multiple candidate-pool retrieval tasks; official Webis data page confirms corpus identity.
limitations: Short arguments; best-counterargument labels are portal-curated and do not encode multi-turn stages or objection types beyond counterargument.
why_relevant: Strongest established baseline for direct counterargument retrieval and negative-candidate construction.

title: Knowledge-Enhanced Evidence Retrieval for Counterargument Generation
authors: Yohan Jo; Haneul Yoo; JinYeong Bak; Alice Oh; Chris Reed; Eduard Hovy
task_description: Retrieve sentence-level counterevidence to a statement, using document retrieval, ranking, sentence selection, and knowledge-enhanced NLI.
inputs: Argumentative statement; Web documents and candidate sentences; CauseNet/Wikidata-enhanced inference.
outputs_or_labels: Counterevidence labels and retrieval rankings; complex causality/example inference cases.
pipeline_gap_filled: objection evidence retrieval; rebuttal support selection
authenticity_class: authentic web evidence plus curated NLI resources
artifact_access_status: official GitHub public; data directory present
license_status: license not stated in repository evidence
evidence_basis: ACL paper states source code/data are available and describes the counterevidence retrieval pipeline; official repository exposes data/counterevidence.
limitations: Targets counterevidence to statements rather than full argument-level rebuttals; evidence provenance and stage labels are not a regulated dialogue protocol.
why_relevant: Useful benchmark for retrieving evidence that can instantiate an objection or rebuttal rather than merely a semantically similar argument.

citation: Kiesel et al. / Touché at CLEF 2025 (2025)
title: Touché at CLEF 2025 — Retrieval-Augmented Debating
authors: Martin Potthast; Henning Wachsmuth; and Touché organizers
task_description: In a four-turn simulated debate, retrieve either counterarguments to the user's utterance or supporting evidence for the attacked system response, then generate the next response.
inputs: User/system utterance sequence U1,S1,U2,S2,U3,S3,U4,S4; approximately 300,000 ClaimRev arguments; training claims.
outputs_or_labels: Next-utterance responses evaluated for Quantity, Quality, Relation, and Manner; toy datasets and TIRA submissions.
pipeline_gap_filled: stage-conditioned disputation retrieval; counterargument-vs-support routing; rebuttal response generation
authenticity_class: authentic argument collection with simulated multi-turn protocol
artifact_access_status: official task page and data/API/index links verified; public access route documented
license_status: license not stated on task page
evidence_basis: Official task page explicitly defines stage sequence, retrieval alternatives, response limit, collection size, and evaluation criteria.
limitations: Evaluation is response-level and shared-task style; retrieval ground truth is not a fully typed scholastic objection taxonomy; user turns are simulated.
why_relevant: Closest located benchmark to stage-conditioned retrieval: retrieval target changes with dialogue role and local attack history.

title: ConQRet: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Argumentation with LLM Judges
authors: Kaustubh D. Dhole; Kai Shu; Eugene Agichtein
task_description: Evaluate retrieval-augmented argumentation over controversial questions, including retrieval effectiveness, argument quality, and groundedness.
inputs: 98 controversial topics; about 6,500 scraped web documents; expert-authored ProCon arguments; stance-conditioned queries.
outputs_or_labels: Relevant-document judgments, stance-conditioned evidence, generated arguments, and fine-grained LLM-judge dimensions.
pipeline_gap_filled: evidence retrieval and grounded argument generation
authenticity_class: authentic expert arguments and public-web evidence
artifact_access_status: official repository and paper available; dataset download gated by repository instructions
evidence_basis: Paper abstract and official repository specify topic/document statistics, evidence pairing, retrieval use, and standalone-RAG applications.
limitations: Not a multi-turn objection/rebuttal protocol; stage is stance (pro/con), not dialogue role or objection type.
why_relevant: Strong evidence-grounding benchmark for counterargument support and provenance, complementary to RAD25.

title: Touché: First Shared Task on Argument Retrieval
authors: Yury Bondarenko; Johannes Kiesel; Alexander Panchenko; Benno Stein; Henning Wachsmuth; Martin Potthast
task_description: Retrieve relevant arguments for controversial topics from a large argument collection using graded relevance judgments.
inputs: Controversial-topic queries; crawled debate-portal and ChangeMyView argument collection.
outputs_or_labels: Not relevant/relevant/highly relevant judgments; shared-task runs and baselines.
pipeline_gap_filled: argument retrieval infrastructure and relevance evaluation
authenticity_class: authentic online debate and forum arguments
artifact_access_status: paper and official task family accessible
license_status: license not stated in artifact evidence
evidence_basis: Paper describes focused crawl, args.me baseline, and argument-retrieval shared task with graded judgments.
limitations: Topic-conditioned rather than stage-conditioned; relevance does not distinguish objection, support, rebuttal, or response role.
why_relevant: Control benchmark for retrieval quality and candidate-pool evaluation before adding stage labels.

title: Overview of PerspectiveArg2024: The First Shared Task on Perspective Argument Retrieval
authors: Neele Falk; Andreas Waldis; Iryna Gurevych
task_description: Retrieve arguments relevant to a query while conditioning on explicit or implicit socio-cultural perspective.
inputs: Queries and arguments with demographic/socio-cultural variables; multilingual argument collection.
outputs_or_labels: Retrieval rankings across explicit-query/corpus, implicit-query, and related perspective scenarios; shared-task results.
authenticity_class: authentic argument text with annotated perspective metadata
artifact_access_status: ACL paper accessible; artifact URL identified from task ecosystem
evidence_basis: ACL abstract explicitly defines three perspective-conditioned retrieval scenarios and reports a multilingual dataset/shared task.
limitations: Perspective is not a discourse stage; no objection/rebuttal move labels or attack-history state.
why_relevant: Provides a tested design pattern for conditioning retrieval on hidden or explicit context variables, transferable to disputation roles.

title: DialFact: A Benchmark for Fact-Checking in Dialogue
authors: Prakhar Gupta; Chien-Sheng Wu; Wenhao Liu; Caiming Xiong
task_description: Detect verifiable claims, retrieve evidence, and classify dialogue responses as supported, refuted, or insufficient information.
inputs: 22,245 conversational claims paired with Wikipedia evidence; dialogue context.
outputs_or_labels: Verifiable-claim labels; evidence snippets; supported/refuted/not-enough-information labels.
pipeline_gap_filled: dialogue-conditioned evidence retrieval and support/refutation classification
authenticity_class: authentic dialogue-derived claims with Wikipedia evidence
artifact_access_status: paper accessible; official artifact availability not verified in this search
evidence_basis: Abstract directly specifies dialogue context, evidence-retrieval subtask, labels, and dataset size.
limitations: Fact-checking is not argumentative counterargument retrieval; no typed objection/rebuttal or stance-generation protocol.
why_relevant: Useful control for separating dialogue context/evidence retrieval from genuine disputation retrieval.

title: RPC-Bench: A Fine-grained Benchmark for Research Paper Comprehension
authors: Yelin Chen; Fanjin Zhang; Suping Sun; Yunhe Pang; Yuanchun Wang; Jian Song; XiaoYan Li; Lei Hou; Shu Zhao; Jie Tang; Juanzi Li
task_description: Evaluate fine-grained comprehension from authentic review-rebuttal exchanges, using QA items and taxonomy aligned to research workflow.
inputs: OpenReview papers plus review-rebuttal exchanges; text and rendered-page inputs.
outputs_or_labels: Human-verified QA pairs; concepts/methods/experiments/claim-verification dimensions; correctness-completeness and conciseness evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: rebuttal-stage evidence/context selection; structured response evaluation
artifact_access_status: official ACL paper, project page, and GitHub; data downloads documented
license_status: license stated for code repository (Apache-2.0); dataset terms need separate check
evidence_basis: ACL and official project sources state review-rebuttal provenance, benchmark scale/taxonomy, and released code/data workflow.
limitations: QA comprehension rather than retrieval ranking; peer-review rebuttal is a specialized disputation domain and does not model scholastic objection stages.
why_relevant: Emerging benchmark for rebuttal-stage context and claim-response alignment; candidate source for response-obligation labels, not a direct retrieval benchmark.

title: ArgumenText: Searching for Arguments in Heterogeneous Sources
authors: Christian Stab; Johannes Daxenberger; Chris Stahlhut; Tristan Miller; Benjamin Schiller; Christopher Tauchmann; Steffen Eger; Iryna Gurevych
task_description: Retrieve sentential arguments for controversial topics from heterogeneous web sources and compare coverage against expert-curated lists.
inputs: Controversial topic query; heterogeneous web sources; expert-curated argument lists.
outputs_or_labels: Ranked argument sentences and coverage/validity analysis; reported 89% coverage of curated arguments.
authenticity_class: authentic heterogeneous web sources and expert lists
artifact_access_status: paper accessible; artifact landing page access not verified
evidence_basis: ACL abstract directly states task, source heterogeneity, and coverage evaluation.
limitations: No counterargument polarity or dialogue stage; primarily a system demonstration rather than a reusable stage-conditioned benchmark.
why_relevant: Negative/control resource for open-domain retrieval and source heterogeneity when building a candidate pool for rebuttal retrieval.

title: ArgBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Computational Argumentation Tasks
authors: Yamen Ajjour; Carlotta Quensel; Nedim Lipka; Henning Wachsmuth
task_description: Unify 33 prior datasets into 46 computational-argumentation tasks covering mining, perspective, quality, reasoning, and generation; includes reusable task files and splits.
inputs: Task-specific argumentation datasets, instructions, and train/validation/test splits.
outputs_or_labels: Task-level labels/outputs for 46 tasks; prompting and leave-one-task-out evaluation setups.
pipeline_gap_filled: benchmark inventory and reusable argumentation controls
authenticity_class: mixed authentic and synthetic sources inherited from component datasets
artifact_access_status: official ACL paper and Webis repositories public
evidence_basis: ACL abstract and official data repository document 33 datasets, 46 tasks, five skills, and released splits.
limitations: Not designed around retrieval ranking or dialogue stages; usefulness depends on whether selected component tasks expose counterargument/perspective relations.
why_relevant: Important current umbrella benchmark for selecting and comparing argumentation controls, but it does not replace a typed stage-conditioned retrieval benchmark.
